text:
pagerbot: INCIDENT 3456 — routing error spike detected; paging oncall (severity: P1)

sam (oncall): seeing 5xx rate up in us-west, lots of fallback to variant-b, latency spikes too. graphs: https://metrics.redwood/3456

lee (sre): confirmed. Smart routing is shunting to fallback variants and then back to standard variants, looks like a sticky loop for ~30s intervals.

nina (runtime): trace sample: 
```
2026-03-15T09:12:10Z request id=abc123 route=chat model=variant-a region=us-west response=timeout fallback->variant-b route=region-eu fallback->variant-c
```

jordan (prod-eng): hmm the fallback policy was changed 30m ago (hotpatch) to prioritize region capacity. Could be the new ordering + aggressive retry is causing oscillation.

ash (cs): we have 2 customers a) AtlasMail (high throughput) b) Shoply (low throughput) reporting errors. CS is watching.

sam (oncall): i pushed a manual hotpatch: forced region us-west to DRAIN to avoid bad hardware node group. command: `rbctl region set us-west state=drain --force`

lee (sre): whoa — draining region while routing policy still prefers us-west will push traffic to other regions and trigger fallbacks. Did you also flip the routing priorities?

sam (oncall): no, i only drained the region because a GPU group was flapping and serving bad KV cache hits. wanted to stop error noise.

nina (runtime): that caused a big spike — traffic redistributed to eu/asia, many requests hit quantized variant-c which isn't fully warmed; KV cache misses cause timeouts -> retries -> routing fallback -> back to us-west when some nodes come online -> sticky routing. loop.

jordan (prod-eng): can we revert the drain? what's the state? `rbctl region get us-west`

sam (oncall): region us-west=drain, draining tasks: 12/12, connection_count: 0. I can un-drain but worried about the flappy nodes.

lee (sre): short term mitigation: 1) stop aggressive fallback retries (policy retries=0 for this route), 2) unblock us-west but mark unhealthy so we avoid cold starts.

nina (runtime): i can push a routing hotfix: set fallback_retries=0 for route:/v1/chat and lower fallback_priority for region-eu by weight -20. Deploying now.

deploy-bot: deploy started by nina for config routing-hotfix-1992 on channel=incidents

sam (oncall): while deploy rolls, i'm going to proto-un-drain us-west but keep nodes cordoned: `rbctl region set us-west state=active --cordon` so no new hosts get scheduled.

ash (cs): customers: AtlasMail shows 12% request error rate, Shoply 7%. CS has informed AtlasMail that we're investigating; they are in a live campaign, escalating.

lee (sre): after the hotfix, check the retry counters and KV cache warm rate. we need to avoid warm-cold thrashing.

deploy-bot: deploy succeeded (routing-hotfix-1992) by nina. change summary: fallback_retries=0, fallback_backoff_ms=3000, region-eu weight -20

nina (runtime): metrics: request 5xx rate falling from 18% -> 4% in 2 minutes. latency still a bit high for queued cold variants.

sam (oncall): i've un-drained us-west to active+cordoned. old nodes still offline but traffic preference should stabilize.

jordan (prod-eng): i'm going to run a manual rollback of the earlier hotpatch that changed routing ordering (the one 30m ago) — we'll move back to pre-hotpatch config but keep the new retry limits. starting rollback now: `rbctl config rollback 2026-03-15-1700-hotpatch`

lee (sre): caution: manual rollbacks can cause compatibility mismatches with warmed KV caches and model variants. coordinate with runtime.

sam (oncall): noticed a small customer-facing blip right after rollback — AtlasMail reported a 2 minute increase in latency. CS on it.

nina (runtime): watching model warmup. We should run an eval sweep on variant-c to ensure outputs are within expected quality; some customers reported odd generation truncation.

ash (cs): AtlasMail says some completions are truncated mid-sentence. they want root cause and ETA.

jordan (prod-eng): investigation notes: sequence = hotpatch reorder -> us-west flapping -> manual drain -> routing oscillation -> manual hotfix (retry=0) -> partial stabilization -> rollback of reorder -> small blip. Root cause: coupling manual region state changes + config reorder without coordination with runtime warming led to fallback oscillation and cold variant exposure.

lee (sre): action items: 1) postmortem with timeline and commands, 2) add guardrails in rbctl: disallow region drain unless routing policy marked safe, 3) add preflight that checks warmed KV cache for variant groups before rollback, 4) CS mitigations: notify impacted customers and run targeted replays to warm variants.

sam (oncall): i'll start the incident doc and collect all commands/logs. pinging @jordan for config diffs and @nina for warmup metrics.

pagerbot: INCIDENT 3456 status changed to MONITORING (owner: sam)

ash (cs): AtlasMail acknowledges ongoing mitigation, wants weekly update. Shoply is fine now.

lee (sre): quick note for the postmortem: don't do unilateral region drains in P1 unless we have a rollback plan for routing.

jordan (prod-eng): will open a PR to add a safety check into the rollout tooling; also we should add a canary for region preference changes (5% traffic).

sam (oncall): closing here, moving to incident doc: https://playbooks.redwood/incidents/3456. will follow up with a full write-up and timeline. thanks all. :thumbsup:
